title: Are LLMs Useful in the Poorest Schools? TheTeacher.AI in Sierra Leone
venue: NeurIPS’23 Workshop on Generative AI for Education (GAIED)
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether large language models can be useful in very low-resource K-12 school systems, especially for teacher support rather than direct student use. The authors focus on the problem that teachers in Sierra Leone often have limited access to professional development, classroom support, and instructional resources, while also facing poor internet connectivity and low device access.

The intervention studied is TheTeacher.AI, a WhatsApp-based GPT-3.5 Turbo chatbot designed to help teachers through conversational support. It was tailored for low-resource conditions and restricted to education-related queries, with added safeguards and pedagogy-oriented prompting. The paper reports early implementation and usage data from an opportunistic pilot across 122 schools and 193 teachers, alongside qualitative observations and analysis of 6,900 teacher queries.

The context is Sierra Leone, a low-income Sub-Saharan African setting where many teachers are unqualified, class sizes are large, and internet access is limited. Teachers used the tool mainly for concept clarification, lesson planning, writing support, professional development, and classroom management. The authors conclude that some teachers found the system valuable and used it regularly, but adoption required training and overcoming access barriers. The paper is primarily descriptive and observational, not causal, and it does not evaluate learning or teaching outcomes directly.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a descriptive field/pilot study with qualitative observations and usage-log analysis, not a controlled causal evaluation. It is peer-reviewed workshop-style evidence, but credibility for impact claims is limited by opportunistic recruitment and lack of comparison group.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper shows promising uptake and practical usefulness in a priority population, but it does not estimate a causal effect on learning or teacher performance. Any impact remains unclear and is inferred from descriptive usage patterns rather than measured outcomes.

interventions.use_case: A WhatsApp-based GPT-3.5 Turbo chatbot (TheTeacher.AI) designed to support K-12 teachers in Sierra Leone with on-demand professional development, including lesson planning, classroom management, concept clarification, and subject-matter questions.

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports sustained teacher use of the chatbot over the school year, with 193 of 240 teachers using it and 6,900 total queries. The main observed benefit was practical support for teachers' work: 21% of queries were for lesson planning, 6% for professional development, and usage peaked during evenings and weekends, suggesting the tool helped with planning and preparation outside instructional time.
finding.measure: Query logs, usage frequency, and topic/task classification of teacher messages

finding.finding_summary: This is an early implementation/field observation paper rather than a causal impact study. It suggests the chatbot may be feasible in low-resource school systems, but also documents substantial implementation barriers including poor connectivity, limited teacher digital skills, and the need for training and human support.
finding.measure: Field observations and qualitative implementation feedback
finding.study_size: n=193 teachers used by data cutoff; pilot across 122 schools
